newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African mkts downgrade expectations from Mandela.
newsitem.headline: S.African mkts downgrade expectations from Mandela.

text.p: South Africa's financial markets were on Friday downgrading expectations of a major announcement on exchange controls from President Nelson Mandela when he opens parliament at 0900 GMT, dealers said.

Political sources told Reuters on Thursday that Mandela's keenly-awaited address was likely to pledge faster implementation of the government's macroeconomic strategy, including privatisation and relaxation of exchange controls.
But while the speech could signal changes in the pipeline, it was not expected to contain any specific measures on dismantling exchange controls, they said.
A more detailed policy statement on controls could come in the March 12 budget.
"I think it will be a damp squib," said one bond trader of Mandela's speech. "I don't think they will announce anything big today, but our markets are still fundamentally positive."
Dealers said the rand and bonds had been feeding on each other recently, with a strong rand tempting overseas buyers back into South African debt and heavy bond buying boosting the currency.
Foreigners were once again heavy buyers of South African bonds on Thursday, taking a net 340.83 million rands worth. Net foreign purchases this year now amount to more than 3.2 billion rand.

Confidence has been restored to South Africa by expectations of a sharply improving trade balance this year which should cut the current account deficit and boost critically low foreign exchange reserves, analysts say.
Gold and foreign exchange reserve figures for January, due at 1600 GMT, are expected to show a substantial improvement on the previous month, reflecting heavy capital inflows.
The consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters is for a rise to a six-month high of 11.2 billion rand from 10.3 billion in December, despite a fall in the value of gold holdings.
At 0600 GMT the rand was trading at 4.4700/4730 against the dollar from 4.4750/4780 at 1400 GMT on Thursday.
The benchmark R150 long bond was yielding 15.115 percent, up from 15.04 percent on Thursday, following a late sell order from one major player on Thursday, dealers said.
